title: Akshay Kumar Quietly Sold Two Mumbai Flats for 7.1 Crore. He Nearly Doubled His Money in Nine Years.
excerpt: The Oberoi Sky City apartments in Borivali appreciated 93 percent since 2017. For NRIs watching Mumbai real estate, the numbers tell a specific story.
body:
Akshay Kumar has quietly sold two residential apartments in Mumbai's Oberoi Sky City project in Borivali East for a combined ₹7.1 crore — nearly double what he paid for them nine years ago. The transactions were registered on June 2, 2026, and the details only surfaced after real estate analytics firm CRE Matrix accessed the property documents. There was no press release, no social media post, no announcement of any kind.

The numbers are instructive. Both units sit on the 35th floor of Tower B within Oberoi Sky City, a premium development on the Western Express Highway. The larger apartment, at 1,101 square feet of carpet area, sold for ₹5.75 crore with two parking spaces. The smaller adjacent unit, 252 square feet, went for ₹1.35 crore with one parking space. Both were purchased by Suvarna Rupeshkumar Sakpal.

## The Returns

Kumar had originally acquired both apartments from Incline Realty Pvt Ltd in November 2017. The larger flat cost ₹3 crore. The smaller one was bought for ₹67.55 lakh. That puts the combined acquisition cost at roughly ₹3.68 crore against a sale price of ₹7.1 crore — an appreciation of approximately 93 percent over eight and a half years. The smaller unit alone appreciated by 99 percent.

These are not exceptional returns by Mumbai real estate standards, but they are consistently strong. And they are part of a pattern. In January 2025, Kumar sold a 1,073-square-foot apartment in the same Borivali area for ₹4.25 crore. Earlier that same month, he offloaded a luxury flat in the Oberoi 360 West project in Worli for ₹80 crore. Earlier this year, he reportedly leased a duplex in an Oberoi complex in Andheri West for ₹1.44 lakh per month.

## Why NRIs Should Read the Fine Print

For the Indian diaspora, particularly those who invested in Mumbai property remotely or are considering it, Kumar's transactions tell a useful story. Borivali East — once considered a distant suburb — has matured into a premium residential market. The Western Express Highway corridor, where Oberoi Sky City sits, has benefited from metro connectivity, commercial development, and the steady migration of upper-middle-class families from cramped South Mumbai apartments to spacious suburban towers.

A 93 percent return over nine years translates to roughly a 7.5 percent compound annual growth rate. That beats fixed deposits but trails the Sensex over the same period. The real advantage for Kumar, as for many high-net-worth investors, is the leverage: he likely financed a portion of the purchase, meaning his actual equity returns are significantly higher.

For NRIs evaluating Mumbai property investments, the lesson is specific. Premium branded developments in suburban micro-markets — Borivali, Goregaon, Thane — continue to appreciate steadily. But the returns are not transformative. They are safe, steady, and predictable, which may be exactly what an NRI looking for a rupee-denominated asset with rental income potential wants.

## The Bigger Picture

Kumar's property portfolio moves also reflect a broader trend among Bollywood's financial elite. Stars are no longer passively accumulating real estate. They are actively managing portfolios — buying, holding, leasing, and selling based on market cycles. Shah Rukh Khan, Amitabh Bachchan, and Deepika Padukone have all made significant real estate transactions in recent years, but Kumar's frequency and consistency stand out.

On the professional front, Kumar is currently preparing for the release of *Welcome To The Jungle*, set to arrive in theatres on June 26, 2026. His real estate exits may simply be smart portfolio rebalancing. Or they may signal that even Bollywood's biggest stars see diminishing marginal returns in Mumbai residential property at current valuations.
